hero.title: One case file, every document.
hero.subtitle: BriefXtract is Intelligent Document Processing (IDP) software that turns the day's post into a case your team can open and check.

what.title: What is BriefXtract?
what.body: BriefXtract is intelligent document processing (IDP) software for debt and social counseling centres and consumer insolvency law firms in Germany, made by Brief Insights in Berlin. A centre or firm scans or forwards the day's post as one mixed PDF. BriefXtract splits it into documents, identifies each one as a letter, court order, invoice, collection letter or notice, and extracts the creditor, file number, amount and due date. Each value is shown beside the line it was read from, so whoever handles the case can check it against the page. Eviction notices, court deadlines and enforcement orders are flagged on arrival. Documents that belong to the same debt are linked into one case record, which can be exported in your format or passed to your case-management system through an API. Processing runs on AWS inside the EU, documents are deleted immediately afterwards, and nothing is used to train a model.

faq.title: Questions centres and law firms ask.
faq.lead: Short answers. The platform, security and results pages have the details.

items.a: The post a counseling centre or law firm receives for a client: letters from creditors, collection letters, invoices, court orders and enforcement notices. Scan or forward them together as one mixed PDF; BriefXtract separates and identifies each document.

items.q: What does BriefXtract extract from a letter?
items.a: The document type, the creditor, the file number, the amount and the due date. Each value keeps a pointer to the line it was read from, and values that need a second look are marked.

items.q: How do we check the results?
items.a: Each extracted field sits beside the line it was read from. To confirm a case, compare the two.

items.q: Does it work with our case-management system?
items.a: BriefXtract returns structured data in the format you need, or connects directly to your case-management system through an API, so nothing has to be retyped.

items.q: Where is client data processed, and is it kept?
items.a: On AWS infrastructure inside the EU, including the AI models on Amazon Bedrock. Documents are deleted immediately after processing and are never used to train a model.

items.q: How much time does BriefXtract save?
items.a: It is designed to bring case preparation from 1 to 8 hours per client down to about 15 minutes. This is a product target and has not yet been measured.

items.title: Returned

items.title: Deleted

items.title: Hosted in the EU
items.body: All processing runs on AWS infrastructure within the EU. No client document leaves the EU.

items.title: Zero data retention
items.body: Documents are permanently deleted immediately after processing. Nothing is stored, indexed or used for training.

items.title: KDG and DSG-EKD
items.body: Compliant with Catholic (KDG) and Protestant (DSG-EKD) data protection law, for Caritas, Diakonie and AWO centres.

items.title: Encrypted, on audited infrastructure
items.body: TLS 1.3 in transit and AES-256 at rest, on enterprise AI infrastructure with full auditability and a 99.9% uptime service level agreement (SLA).

items.title: Professional secrecy
items.body: For law firms, Brief Insights signs a confidentiality agreement under section 43e of the Federal Lawyers' Act (BRAO), covering the duty of secrecy in section 203 of the Criminal Code (StGB).

faq.title: Questions data protection officers and law firms ask.

items.a: Inside the EU, on AWS infrastructure, for the duration of processing only. The extracted case is returned to your system and the source document is deleted. Nothing is kept afterwards.

items.q: Do client documents train your models?
items.a: No. Client data never trains AI models. Documents are processed, returned as a structured case and permanently deleted.

items.q: Will you sign a data processing agreement?
items.a: Yes. A full data processing agreement under GDPR Article 28 is available on request. Ask for it in your demo request.

items.q: Will you sign a confidentiality agreement under § 43e BRAO?
items.a: Yes. For law firms, Brief Insights signs a confidentiality agreement under section 43e of the Federal Lawyers' Act (BRAO), which obliges it to secrecy and sets out the criminal liability under section 203 of the Criminal Code (StGB). It comes in addition to the data processing agreement under GDPR Article 28.

items.q: Does this satisfy KDG and DSG-EKD?
items.a: Yes. BriefXtract is compliant with Catholic (KDG) and Protestant (DSG-EKD) data protection law, and was built for Caritas, Diakonie and AWO centres.
All processing runs on AWS infrastructure within the EU, including the AI models, which run on Amazon Bedrock.

why.title: Why Brief Insights exists.
why.p1: Nine per cent of people in Germany are in debt. The people who help them often spend the first hours of a case opening envelopes. Thirty to eighty letters arrive per client, including court orders, enforcement notices, invoices and collection letters, and each one is sorted, read and retyped by hand before advice can start.
why.p2: Brief Insights was founded in Berlin to take that work off the desk. BriefXtract reads the post, extracts the fields that matter and files each document against the case, so the time spent sorting goes to the client instead.
